topics.topic: Required behavior when orphan value bytes cannot be verified or removed at startup
questions: What happens when an unreferenced value-byte file cannot be removed: does start fail, does the kernel start while never serving it, or is another action required?
If an unreferenced value-byte file cannot be verified or removed at startup, does the kernel refuse to start, continue while leaving it unserved, or take another action?
What happens when an unreferenced value-byte file cannot be removed: must startup fail, or may startup continue as it explicitly may for an unremovable spool directory?

judgement.why: P11 already judged the same question about failures during startup orphan and temporary-file cleanup, and neither the relevant later text nor the reopening change altered it.

precedent.topic: Handling failures during startup orphan and temporary-file cleanup
quotes: open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on a lock file inside data_directory, opened without following links and held for the life of the process; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then remove the module's own temporary files left by an interrupted publish and every file of the content-addressed area whose digest no StoredValue and no file fixture record names, and create the database schema, the content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.

run_start_sequence: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Every step is required: the first step that raises — InstallationRejectedError, RefusedError from the instance check, a store refusal, SandboxUnavailableError, StopRequiredError or any other exception — stops the sequence there and propagates unchanged to the caller with the step named in its reason; no later step runs and nothing is retried or skipped.
precedent.why: The later contracts require open_store to stop on its first failure and require any exception from that startup step to stop the entire start sequence.

topics.topic: Startup ordering and prerequisites for orphan-value cleanup relative to locking, database view, and recovery
questions: At what exact point in startup is orphan-value discovery and removal performed, and must the exclusive data-directory lock and a stable committed database view be acquired first?
Does orphan-value cleanup occur before or after A14 startup recovery, which can rerun work and cause equal orphan bytes to become named?

quotes: open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on a lock file inside data_directory, opened without following links and held for the life of the process; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then remove the module's own temporary files left by an interrupted publish and every file of the content-addressed area whose digest no StoredValue and no file fixture record names, and create the database schema, the content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.

run_start_sequence: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST call, in exactly this order and each exactly once: load_installation with config_path; check_installed_instances with the loaded Installation; open_store with that Installation's data_directory; probe_sandbox; recover_in_flight_attempts; recover_running_runs (A03 rule 8, A09 rule 1, A14 rule 5, A18).
judgement.why: The later contracts place orphan discovery and removal inside open_store after acquisition of the exclusive lock and before sandbox probing and both recovery operations.

topics.topic: Whether startup orphan cleanup includes unreferenced trial-fixture files
questions: When adding or capturing a trial case publishes a file fixture but the store call fails before recording it, must the unreferenced fixture be removed at the next start, retained indefinitely, or treated as a start failure?
Does startup also remove an unreferenced trial-fixture file published by a failed call, or does "value bytes" exclude the separately named file-fixture area?

judgement.why: P25 already judged the same question and established that startup cleanup covers content-addressed files named by neither a StoredValue nor a file-fixture record.

precedent.topic: Startup cleanup policy for unreferenced trial-fixture blobs
quotes: open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on a lock file inside data_directory, opened without following links and held for the life of the process; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then remove the module's own temporary files left by an interrupted publish and every file of the content-addressed area whose digest no StoredValue and no file fixture record names, and create the database schema, the content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.
precedent.why: The later startup note explicitly removes content-addressed files whose digest is named by neither a StoredValue nor a file-fixture record.

topics.topic: Whether orphan value bytes must be removed at run end or may remain until restart
questions: May unreferenced value bytes left by a failed call remain after the associated run ends until the next process start, or must they be removed when the run ends so that they do not outlive it?

topics.topic: Which durable references make value bytes named and exempt from cleanup
questions: Exactly which durable references make value bytes "named" and therefore exempt from removal?
